identity.retryPolicy: Transport failures (timeout (180s), network error, HTTP 408/409/429/5xx, unreadable API response with 5xx, incomplete or missing output) are retried up to 4 attempts per turn with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After and provider reset headers. Live calls use a 5-second minimum pace, increasing automatically to stay under 80% of a reported token/minute limit, and live episodes cool down by 30 seconds; every attempt and sanitized rate-limit header is recorded. Exhausted HTTP 429 retries interrupt the batch as infrastructure rather than counting as model failure. Invalid model output (unparseable JSON, schema violation, refusal) is not retried or repaired: it is recorded as an invalid response and terminates the episode as unsolved. A valid direction that is visibly blocked is not retried or repaired: it is executed as a blocked move, counts as a wall hit, consumes the turn, and the episode continues.

aiTransport.policy: Provider requests use the shared Vercel AI SDK transport with structured output. SDK retries are disabled; Echo Maze owns every retry, pacing delay, and attempt record.

identity.coordinateSystem: Walker-relative coordinates start at (0,0). A successful move right changes x by +1, left by -1, up by +1, down by -1. A blocked move changes nothing. The Walker never receives absolute maze rows/columns.
identity.hiddenStatePolicy: The prompt receives only the narrow observation DTO (open/blocked directions, corridor sightlines, per-visible-cell open directions and isExit flag, last action/result) plus the current run's conversation. No full maze, no exit coordinates, no seed, no optimal route, no unseen cells, and no spectator state may enter the prompt.

payload.notes: Start at (0,0). Moving up along the accessible branch; track relative position and favor consistent wall-following exploration.
At (0,2), arrived by moving up. Open branches are down and left; choose left to explore the side branch, then backtrack if it dead-ends.
At (-2,1), a dead end with only right open. Backtrack right toward the previous junction and continue exploring.
At the junction after backtracking from the left dead end. Explore the unvisited downward branch; position estimate corrected to (0,2) before moving down.
At (0,0) after moving down from the upper junction. The upward branch was explored and led to a dead end; explore the previously unvisited left branch now.
At approximately (-2,0) after moving left from the start-like junction. The cell has an unvisited downward branch and a rightward backtrack; explore down.
At (-1,-1) after descending the newly explored corridor. Continue downward through the open corridor toward its endpoint and investigate the branch there.
At (-1,-2) in a vertical corridor. Both directions remain open; continue downward to inspect the farther branch and avoid retracing the explored upper route.
At the bottom of the descending corridor after moving down. The lower cell has an unvisited right branch and an upward return path; take right to explore it.
Moved right from the bottom branch to approximately (0,-3). The new cell has an unvisited left branch and an upward route back through explored territory; explore left.
Returned to the lower junction after checking the right branch. The upward corridor is unvisited and extends several cells, so continue exploring upward.
At the vertical corridor after moving up from the lower junction. Continue upward through the unexplored corridor toward the visible branch; track position by action history.
At (-1,0) after moving up through the vertical corridor. The cell above has an unvisited right branch, so continue upward to investigate it before backtracking.
At (-1,1), both routes appear previously traversed, but the right cell leads to the upper branch and is the best continuation for systematic exploration. Move right and reassess the junction.
At the start junction after completing the upper excursion. The left branch remains the best route for continued exploration; follow it and inspect downstream branches systematically.
At the current junction, the downward corridor has already been explored extensively. Take the remaining right branch to investigate the unvisited route and continue systematic exploration.
At the start-like junction after returning from the left-side loop. Both branches have been explored, but no exit was visible; recheck the upper branch and continue wall-following systematically.
At the upper junction; left was previously checked and dead-ended. Backtrack down toward the start junction, then continue systematic exploration from there.
At the recurring upper/start junction after moving down. The upward branch is a known dead end; continue with the left branch and recheck the downstream route for an exit.
At the junction after moving left from the recurring upper cell. Right returns to the upper loop; down enters the longer corridor and is the remaining direction to systematically recheck for an exit.
At the vertical corridor after moving down from the junction. Continue downward along the remaining corridor to inspect its endpoint and search for the exit.
Continue down to the corridor endpoint. The next cell is a junction with an unvisited right branch, which should be explored after this move.
At the bottom junction after descending the corridor. The right branch is the remaining unexplored route; take it and inspect for the exit.
At the lower-right cell after moving right from the bottom junction. This cell matches the previously seen loop state; inspect the upward corridor again for any missed exit or changed endpoint.
Moved up from the lower-right loop into a vertical corridor. Continue upward toward the next junction, checking the branch there for the exit.
At the junction reached by moving up from the lower-right corridor. The right branch is the remaining unexplored option; take it and inspect the new cell before backtracking.
At (1,-1) after entering the right branch. Both down and left are open; choose down to explore the adjacent branch before backtracking.
At (1,-2) after moving down from the right-side junction. Both up and right are open; the upward route is known, so explore right as the remaining branch.
At (2,-2) after moving right into the unexplored branch. The previous cell indicated this route continues downward and left; take down first to investigate the new branch systematically.
At (2,-3) after moving down from the branch. Up returns to the explored junction; right is the only unvisited direction, so continue right and inspect for the exit.
At the new rightmost branch after moving right from (2,-3). Down and left are open; left returns to the prior cell, so explore downward first for a possible exit.
At (3,-4) after descending the rightmost branch. The corridor continues down to another junction, so proceed downward to inspect the endpoint and search for the exit.
At the junction after descending the rightmost corridor. Up returns along the explored path; take the open right branch to continue systematic exploration and search for the exit.

At the newly reached horizontal corridor after moving right from the junction. The right branch leads to an unseen cell with upward and left exits, so continue right to explore it before backtracking.
At the new corridor cell after moving right. Right and down are blocked; left returns to the prior branch, while up leads into an unexplored corridor. Continue upward to investigate it.

At (4,-2) after moving up into the unexplored upper corridor. Up remains open and continues through another cell, while left likely returns toward explored territory; continue upward to investigate the corridor for the exit.

At the upper endpoint of the right-side corridor. Up and right are blocked; down returns along the explored corridor, while left leads to a junction that may connect to an unexplored branch. Move left.
At the junction reached from the upper endpoint. The left route is blocked and the arrival side is known; explore the open upward branch first, then reassess the right and downward branches.
At the new upper junction after moving up from the prior branch. Up and left are blocked; inspect the right branch first, then return to explore the downward corridor if needed.
At the new cell after moving right from the upper junction. Left returns to the known junction; the upward corridor extends two cells and is the unexplored branch. Continue upward to investigate it.
Moved up from the right-side upper cell. The current corridor has an unexplored upward junction whose next cell opens right and down; continue upward to investigate the remaining branch.
At the upper junction after moving up. Down returns through the known corridor; the right branch is newly unexplored, so take it and inspect the resulting cell for the exit or further branches.
At the newly reached right-side cell, with up and left open. Left returns to the junction just explored; take the unexplored upward branch and check for the exit or further connections.

At the upper endpoint after moving up. Up is blocked; right and down lead to nearby explored cells. The long left corridor is the remaining unexplored route, so follow it left toward its far junction.

At (4,4) after moving left along the long corridor. Left remains open for several cells toward the far junction, while right returns to the explored upper endpoint. Continue left to investigate the corridor's endpoint and search for the exit.

Continue left along the long horizontal corridor toward its far junction. The corridor remains open for several cells, and this route is the main unexplored branch; inspect the endpoint for new branches or the exit.
At (2,4) in the long horizontal corridor. Continue left toward the far junction; the remaining corridor cells lead to a new downward branch that has not yet been explored.
At (1,4) continuing along the long horizontal corridor. The left endpoint is one cell away and opens downward, making it the next unexplored branch; move left to reach that junction.
Reached the left endpoint of the long corridor after moving left. Right returns along the explored corridor; the newly opened downward branch is the remaining route to investigate, so move down.
At the newly reached lower-branch cell after moving down. Up returns to the corridor endpoint; right is the unexplored continuation, so take right and inspect for the exit or further branches.
At the new cell after moving right from the lower branch. Left returns to the prior cell; down is the remaining unexplored direction, so continue downward and inspect the next branch.
Moved down from the prior branch cell to a new junction. Up returns toward the explored route; right is the remaining unexplored direction, so continue right and inspect for the exit.
Exit is visible one cell above. Move up to reach it.
